purpose: Give every graphic family the same structural deliverable set while keeping its typefaces, palette, identity assets, accents, and capability decisions local to that family.
parity_policy: Every family inherits the same five baseline output slots: one-page document, two-page document, responsive light-context web page, product slick, and six-page component proof.
Every baseline output uses the light context. Light describes the surface and contrast treatment; it is not an extra family or a separate product slot.
Each family records evidence or an explicit blocked/not-run state for every slot; a missing output is never silently treated as parity.
The shared hierarchy and composition rules may be reused. Font selections, marks, colors, illustrations, and accent motifs may not be borrowed across families.

A family may express an accent through its own dividers, markers, frames, panels, or data treatments; each accent needs a semantic or navigational job and must remain distinct from the shared structural rules.
Output readiness is independent from route selection, publication clearance, browser verification, print approval, and whole-brand approval.

family_output_parity.policy: The six named families use the same output slot IDs and structural contract. They may use different profile-owned typefaces, accents, assets, page geometry, and content. An absent or held artifact remains a visible coverage gap.

typography_role_policy.mapping_contract: Every PDF and web exporter requires exactly one role_map entry for each shared_typography_roles item. Each semantic role selects its mapped, declared physical face. PDF adapters must use those semantic selectors for every exercised role; validating a map without applying it is insufficient. Font files, sizes, spacing, colors, and visual treatment remain family-owned.
typography_role_policy.physical_face_policy: Suite 0.5 adds optional mono while preserving existing body/display/strong and optional wordmark profiles. A role may map only to a supported physical face explicitly declared by that family. Optional face IDs have no automatic fallback; profiles without them map all 17 semantic roles to their other declared faces.
typography_role_policy.pdf_role_selector_policy: Generate one TeX font selector for all 17 semantic roles from the family's role_map. The selectors bind only to the family's physical font commands; composition adapters own size and spacing. Changing a semantic mapping must change its emitted PDF font selector without editing layout code.
typography_role_policy.unresolved_type_policy: A neutral system face may be used for layout metrics only when the profile records type as unresolved. Such a proof cannot be treated as a typeface selection.

profile_owned_accent_slots.purpose: Identify a section or sequence step; pair shape or text with color.
Separate related blocks or signal a change in reading mode.
Bring a supporting note forward without making every paragraph a card.
Distinguish series and states with labels, shapes, or patterns as well as color.
Repeat a family-owned mark or motif at a measured scale.
Help readers locate a section, continuation, or page state.

long_form_document_components.implementation_rule: Every adapter supports the semantic structure below while keeping typography, identity, palette, accents, and page geometry in its own family profile. Components may share layout logic; they must use family-owned visual tokens. The same source text should be used when two visual routes are compared.

requirements: page references generated from final pagination
source text shared across visual route comparisons
at least one resolved in-text cross-reference
repeated header when a table spans pages
explicitly fictional or source-backed data status
cited records resolve to a bibliography
separate appendix heading and referenceable page entry
numbered note appears on its source page
duplex inner/outer convention recorded when applicable
variant has a textual label and meaning beyond color
cards do not flatten all body prose into panels

verification: inspect final references and generated contents page
check font embedding and output color intent
reject overfull text and unresolved references

baseline_outputs.duplex: long-edge when intended for print; inner/outer geometry is explicit

baseline_outputs.page_count: 1 or 2, declared by the profile recipe

light_context_policy: Light is an output context applied consistently across the baseline suite. It is not a typeface or a separate identity. Additional dark or print contexts remain profile-specific and explicit.

status_legend.verified_local_build: The exact profile recipe, source record, generated output, hashes, and build checks are present.
status_legend.static_unverified: Source or static output exists; browser behavior or target rendering is not verified.
status_legend.source_only: A relevant source specimen exists but does not satisfy the complete baseline output.
status_legend.held_route: The profile is held; do not invent a route or output.
status_legend.reviewed_local_build: A recipe, local build report, SHA-256-pinned output, and screen rendering review are recorded. This does not imply a separate test-suite ID, browser verification, print approval, release clearance, or whole-family approval.

profile_specificity: Exact typefaces, colors, identity assets, accents, and rights are resolved in each system's own profile and source record. The common contract supplies structure only and does not publish or select brand values.
